name: Queen Anne Playhouse
description: A 1:24 Queen Anne playhouse with a tower, a front gable, lift-out panels, and lift-off roofs. The viewer places the CAD STLs.

target_printer.bed_source: Project brief envelope 330 x 320 x 325 mm. Not re-measured on a machine.
target_printer.brim_allowance_mm: Parts are limited to 310 x 300 x 315 so 10 mm remains on each XY side and 10 mm in Z.

mechanism.panels: Lift 8.6 mm to clear the lower hook and the head fin, then pull out along the wall normal. Removable. No hinges, magnets, or loose pins.
mechanism.balcony: Saddles over two ledges on the tower plate and lifts off upward. The rail sits beyond the panel pull, so the panel path stays clear.
mechanism.roofs: Gravity plug into the plate opening. Lift straight up.
mechanism.rear_shear: Tongued into the rear posts and captured by the floor and the plate. It is structure, not a play panel.
mechanism.inter_bay: Underside lap on each base and each upper floor, 16 mm long, 0.40 mm side clearance. Plates are located by the posts. Interior sides between bays are open above the corner posts.

legacy_interface.peg_orientation: tip down, flange underside on the deck (z translation +11 after a 180 degree X rotation)
legacy_interface.conclusion: The legacy floor tile STL is 127 x 127 x 10 mm. A tip-down snap_post_v0 intersects that tile by ~0 mm^3 at all 16 measured sockets and by a large volume 10 mm off the grid, so the Ø6 peg / Ø6.3 socket interface is real. One Queen Anne bay is exactly two measured tile-widths in X and is not two tile-depths in Y. The same peg intersects the Queen Anne floor, which has no Ø6.3 socket. The kits share a 254 mm module width and do not share a joint.

limits: Not printed. Clearances are CAD targets.
Forces, buckling, floor deflection, lap shear, fatigue, and tip-over were not calculated or tested.
No load rating and no toy-safety certification.
Do not treat the assembled house as a lifting handle.
Generic brim-allowance check only. No slicer was run. Not an H3C test.
Panel edges are square. Pinch gaps and finger comfort were not trialed.
The balcony must come off before the second-storey tower front panel is fully pulled.
